title: The Witkoff family's own Gulf money
summary: The core of the lead is documented. Qatar's sovereign fund (QIA) bought the Park Lane Hotel for about $623M in August 2023. Alex Witkoff pitched QIA a planned $4B real-estate credit fund, and per the NYT the sons also approached UAE and Kuwaiti funds. Steve Witkoff disclosed a $120M sale of a Witkoff Group stake with no buyer, date or percentage named, and his disclosures went uncertified while Congress pressed for investigations. Corrections: the Park Lane seller was a Witkoff–Mubadala joint venture, and Qatar says the hotel was not Witkoff's. The QIA pitch dates to 2024, not 2025, and QIA declined, so the fund was shelved. The NYT's separate claim of $100M from a Qatar-part-owned Apollo trust was corrected: the lender was Apollo itself. No source shows the family's business influenced Gaza, Qatar, Iran or Russia diplomacy.

sub_claims.statement: Qatar's sovereign fund bought the Witkoff Group's Park Lane hotel stake in 2023.
sub_claims.finding: In August 2023 QIA bought the Park Lane Hotel at 36 Central Park South for about $623M ($622.9M) in an entity-level deal, with $400M of financing from Athene, Apollo's annuity arm. The seller was a joint venture of Witkoff and Abu Dhabi's Mubadala. Mubadala had bought Jho Low's roughly 38% stake from the DOJ for $139.6M in 2018, and the 2013 purchase price was about $654M. Witkoff's share at the sale was not disclosed. Qatar's International Media Office says the hotel was not owned by Witkoff or his companies, and Witkoff says he partnered with Mubadala, never with QIA.

sub_claims.statement: Alex and Zach Witkoff sought billions from Qatar, UAE and Kuwait sovereign funds for real-estate vehicles in 2025.
sub_claims.finding: The NYT (2025-09-26, Kamin and Hope) reported that the sons sought billions from sovereign funds in Qatar, the UAE and Kuwait. The vehicle was a proposed $4B 'Special Situations Real Estate Credit Fund' expected to earn about $80M a year in fees. QIA spokeswoman Melanie Dunn confirmed that Alex pitched QIA, in 2024, and said QIA declined. The UAE and Kuwait approaches rest on the NYT alone. The Witkoff Group called the plans preliminary and shelved. The NYT originally reported that the Witkoff Group received $100M (as recently as May 2025) from an Apollo-run trust partly owned by Qatar. That link has since been corrected: per a correction relayed by the Jerusalem Post, the lender on the Belgrove property loan was Apollo Global Management itself, not the subsidiary in which Qatar had invested. The family's lawyer (Parlatore) said Athene, Apollo's insurance arm, made the loan and has no QIA ownership or control. QIA told the NYT it was not invested in the Brook or Belgrove properties, and Apollo says its investors do not direct its investments. The Witkoff family and the Witkoff Group threatened the NYT with a defamation suit over the article. No filed suit was found. See C73.

sub_claims.statement: Steve Witkoff sold a stake in his firm for about $120M, with no buyer named.
sub_claims.finding: Bloomberg reported on 2025-09-15/16, from his OGE disclosure, that he sold a Witkoff Group stake for $120M. The filing gave no buyer, date or percentage. A spokesperson says he remains a minority shareholder with no operating role since 2024, and Alex runs the firm. Witkoff first said in March 2025 that he was divesting. No buyer identity surfaced through Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Witkoff's ethics agreement and disclosures leave the Gulf conflicts unresolved.
sub_claims.finding: No published ethics agreement surfaced. Warren and Murphy (2025-11-18) said no ethics official had signed his disclosure, and asked about divestment and waivers. Schiff and seven other senators (2025-10-22) pressed him on his WLF assets. Meeks, Amo and Garcia (2026-01-08) asked the State and Commerce IGs and OGE to investigate him over the UAE AI-chip deal overlapping WLF's Emirati deal. No IG outcome was found. The WLF income and divestment questions are covered in C14 and C42.

sub_claims.statement: The family's Gulf money overlaps with Witkoff's Gaza, Qatar, Iran and Russia negotiations, including the Qatar jet and the Doha strike aftermath.
sub_claims.finding: The overlap in time is real. He led the January and October 2025 Gaza ceasefire talks with Qatar as mediator, and the NYT story ran in between. On the 2025-09-09 Israeli strike on Doha, the White House said Witkoff warned Qatar in advance, while Qatar said the call came about 10 minutes after the strike began. No source shows any business tie influenced policy. Qatar says investment is kept separate from diplomacy. On Russia, Byline Times reports an undisclosed real-estate tie to Leonard Blavatnik, and Witkoff's spokeswoman denies any financial stake in the Russian asset talks.

corrections: The brief says Qatar bought 'the Witkoff Group's Park Lane hotel stake'. In fact QIA bought the whole hotel (about $623M, Aug 2023) from a Witkoff–Mubadala JV. Witkoff's share is undisclosed, and Qatar says the hotel was not owned by Witkoff or his companies.
The brief dates the sons' fundraising to 2025. QIA dates Alex's pitch to 2024, before Witkoff took office. The NYT reported it in Sept 2025, and QIA declined, so the fund was shelved.
The brief names 'Alex/Zach'. Only Alex's approach to QIA is confirmed by the counterparty. Zach's role and the UAE and Kuwait approaches rest on NYT sourcing.

The NYT's '$100M from an Apollo-run trust partly owned by Qatar' was corrected. Per the correction relayed by the Jerusalem Post, the lender on the Belgrove loan was Apollo Global Management, not the Qatar-invested subsidiary. No Qatari money in that loan is documented (see C73).
denials_and_context: Qatar's International Media Office (2025-09-27) called the NYT's claim that Qatar cultivated Witkoff false and 'absurd', and said Qatari entities had dealt with him for years before Trump's election.

The Witkoff family's lawyer, Timothy Parlatore, threatened the NYT with a defamation suit on 2025-10-02 and demanded a retraction. No suit was found. The NYT corrected a lender name on a separate (Belgrove) loan.
Apollo says its investors do not direct its investments. The White House counsel says Witkoff takes ethics compliance seriously.

Against the family: the disclosures were uncertified, the $120M buyer is unnamed, and his son runs a firm that takes Qatar-linked capital. For the family: the QIA pitch predates his appointment and was rejected, and the Park Lane sale predates his government role.

The Witkoff family and Witkoff Group threatened the NYT with a defamation suit over the 26 Sep 2025 article and demanded corrections. QIA denies investing in the Brook or Belgrove, and the White House called the story a 'bogus smear'.

changes: Corrected the $100M item in sub-claim 2, the summary, corrections, the Apollo entity, relationships and the lead. A correction relayed by the Jerusalem Post says the Belgrove loan's lender was Apollo Global Management, not the Qatar-invested subsidiary. The family lawyer says Athene made it, and QIA denies investing in the Brook or Belgrove. This reconciles with C73. The Apollo-to-Witkoff Group edge is now 'commercial', not Qatar money.
Added the Witkoff family's threatened defamation suit against the NYT and its demand for corrections. No filed suit was found.

Park Lane, the QIA pitch (2024, declined, QIA spokeswoman Melanie Dunn) and the $120M sale (Sep 2025 disclosure, no buyer through Nov 2026) re-confirmed via Gulf Times, The Real Deal, Bisnow and Forbes coverage. Verdict and confidence unchanged.
